metadata.name: TrustGuard AI - Caller ID Verification Directory
metadata.supersedes: v1 fictional-only directory (v1 entries preserved under fictional_banks)
metadata.purpose: Caller-ID verification database for scam detection. When a caller claims to represent an organization (by name, abbreviation or alias), match the claim against this directory; if the caller's number does not match any official number listed for that organization, surface the entry's 'warning' and apply Family-A impersonation scoring.
metadata.demo_policy: All demo transcripts, recordings and training scenarios use FICTIONAL institutions only (see fictional_banks; Build Bible Section 17). The real names and numbers in 'organizations' are used exclusively for verification lookups and are never used to generate demo or training content.

normalization.description: Normalize both the incoming caller ID and the directory numbers before comparing.
steps: Strip all characters except digits and a leading '+'
Map letters to telephone keypad digits (ABC=2, DEF=3, GHI=4, JKL=5, MNO=6, PQRS=7, TUV=8, WXYZ=9) so vanity numbers such as +92-21-111-APNA-00 become +92-21-111-2762-00
Drop the country-code prefix '92' and the trunk prefix '0'; compare the trailing 9-10 digits
A claim is verified only when BOTH the claimed organization matches (name / short_name / alias, case-insensitive) AND the normalized caller number equals one of that organization's official_numbers
Some organizations legitimately share helplines or number formats (e.g., MCB and MCB Islamic, SNGPL and SSGC, HBL and HabibMetro); the claimed organization's own entry governs the lookup
3-5 digit shortcodes (3737, 4444, 786, 345, 310, 333, 123, 555, 1218, ...) are valid for SMS sender comparison only - a voice call can never legitimately originate from a shortcode

verification_logic: Claimed organization found AND caller number matches an official number (normalized) -> emit the platform_official_channel counter-signal (legitimate official channel, taxonomy Family D).

Claimed organization found AND caller number does NOT match any official number -> surface the entry's warning and score the impersonation label for the entry's category: bank_impersonation, wallet_impersonation, telecom_impersonation, government_impersonation, utility_impersonation, courier_impersonation or tech_support_impersonation (Family A).

Caller ID matches a suspicious_pattern (e.g., a +92-3XX mobile number) while claiming any organization in this directory -> escalate: banks, wallets, government agencies and utilities never place official outbound calls from personal mobile numbers.
No organization claimed -> apply suspicious_patterns to the raw caller ID alone (weak signal only).
fictional_banks entries must NEVER produce real-world verification verdicts; they exist only to keep training/demo data isolated from real verification targets.
metadata.disclaimer: Numbers compiled from publicly listed official helplines, UANs and shortcodes for anti-fraud verification. Helplines change over time - re-verify against each organization's official website before production use. This file is not an authorized communication from any listed organization.
metadata.maintenance: Re-verify all numbers quarterly; on any change, update the entry, bump 'version' (minor) and refresh 'last_updated'.

suspicious_patterns.description: Pakistani mobile number (+92-3XX-XXXXXXX / 03XX-XXXXXXX). Banks, wallets, government agencies and utilities never initiate official outbound customer calls from personal mobile numbers - the single strongest caller-ID red flag.
suspicious_patterns.note: Map to the impersonation label of whatever category the caller claims (bank_impersonation, wallet_impersonation, government_impersonation, utility_impersonation). Caller-ID layer signal only - final score depends on what the caller asks for; a mobile claim plus any credential/payment request is the classic Pakistani vishing pattern. Courier and telco mobile calls are lower confidence (riders and some marketing legitimately use mobiles) - require an accompanying fee demand or credential request.

suspicious_patterns.description: Jazz-owned mobile series (0300-0309 and 0320-0329). Attribution signal: a caller claiming to be Telenor, Zong or Ufone while calling from a Jazz-series number is a double mismatch.
suspicious_patterns.note: Operator attribution only - do not score on the series alone; combine with the claimed organization.

suspicious_patterns.description: Zong-owned mobile series (0310-0319). Attribution signal for cross-checking a claimed telecom identity.
suspicious_patterns.note: Operator attribution only - combine with the claimed organization.

suspicious_patterns.description: Ufone-owned mobile series (0330-0339). Attribution signal for cross-checking a claimed telecom identity.
suspicious_patterns.note: Operator attribution only - combine with the claimed organization.

suspicious_patterns.description: Telenor-owned mobile series (0340-0359). Attribution signal for cross-checking a claimed telecom identity.
suspicious_patterns.note: Operator attribution only - combine with the claimed organization.

suspicious_patterns.description: International (non-Pakistani) number. Pakistani banks, wallets, government agencies, utilities and couriers have no reason to call customers from foreign numbers.
suspicious_patterns.note: Common in refund and tech-support scams routed through foreign VoIP providers. Map to the impersonation label of the claimed category.

suspicious_patterns.description: Caller ID displayed in the official UAN style (111-XXX-XXX or 0XX-111-XXX-XXX). The format alone does NOT prove legitimacy - UAN spoofing is trivial. Always require an independent callback to the directory number.
suspicious_patterns.note: If the displayed number exactly matches a directory official_number (normalized) it may count as platform_official_channel; if it merely looks like a UAN but is not listed for the claimed organization, treat it as spoofed and escalate.

suspicious_patterns.description: Ordinary city landline (0XX-XXXXXXX / 0XX-XXXX-XXXX). Banks and large organizations publish UAN-style helplines; a random landline claiming to be a head-office or helpline callback is suspicious unless it exactly matches this directory.
suspicious_patterns.note: Some directory entries legitimately list landlines (e.g., ZTBL 051-920-4091, PPCB 042-992-11201, SBP 021-992-1151) - always compare against official_numbers after normalization.

suspicious_patterns.description: Hidden, masked or garbage caller ID ('Unknown', 'Private', '***', 'XXXX'). Banks and government agencies do not hide their numbers.
suspicious_patterns.note: Combine with any impersonation claim - hidden ID plus an authority claim is a classic scam pattern.

suspicious_patterns.description: 3-5 digit number presented as a VOICE caller ID. Shortcodes (3737, 4444, 345, 1218, ...) are SMS-only channels; a voice call can never legitimately originate from a shortcode.
suspicious_patterns.note: Guaranteed spoofing. Surface the warning of whichever organization the caller claims.

suspicious_patterns.description: A run of 8 or more identical digits in the caller ID (e.g., 0300-0000000) - typical of spoofing tools and fake numbers.
suspicious_patterns.note: No official number in this directory contains an 8-digit run; official numbers such as 051-111-111-425 (7-run) are deliberately not matched.

suspicious_patterns.description: Sequential digit runs (1234567890, 0123456789, 9876543210) - fake or spoofed caller IDs.
suspicious_patterns.note: Low severity alone; combine with a claimed organization or credential request.

suspicious_patterns.description: +92 number with a wrong digit count - malformed caller IDs generated by spoofing tools.
suspicious_patterns.note: Valid Pakistani numbers are +92 followed by 9-10 digits (mobile 3XXXXXXXXX; landline city code plus 7-8 digits).

suspicious_patterns.description: Mobile number written with inserted separators, dots or spaced digits inside a message ('+ 9 2 3 0 0 ...', '03.00.1234567') - scammers obfuscate numbers to evade keyword filters and redirect victims to a callback mobile.
suspicious_patterns.note: Any message asking you to call a mobile number 'for the bank' or 'for support' is redirection - official channels never route callbacks to personal mobiles. Map to verification_avoidance or payment_redirection depending on context.

suspicious_patterns.description: WhatsApp deep-links (wa.me / api.whatsapp.com) to a raw phone number - scammers move victims off recorded official channels to WhatsApp.
suspicious_patterns.note: platform_migration in the scoring taxonomy; escalate when combined with an impersonation claim or credential request.

suspicious_patterns.description: Alphanumeric SMS sender ID carrying an organization name plus extra look-alike suffix characters (e.g., 'HBLVerify', 'JazzCash-Award', 'NADRA-Check'). Legitimate sender IDs never carry added suffixes; exact matches to well-known senders do not trigger this pattern.
suspicious_patterns.note: Apply to the SMS sender ID field only. Fire as high-confidence ONLY when combined with a credential request, fee demand or link in the message body; a spoofed sender ID plus an OTP request is otp_harvesting + bank_impersonation. Bare exact sender tokens (e.g., 'HBL') do not match this pattern and require corroboration.
